findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct or drop the 'tracker ticket's rebar-version field' source in Approach (b): rebar tickets have no such field (rebar-version is the attestation-manifest gate stamp, not a ticket field); specify a real per-ticket source for the reported-against SHA/version or restrict (b) to reports that carry rebar --version.
evidence: Approach: 'the version the bug was reported against (the rebar --version / commit sha in the report, or the tracker ticket's rebar-version field)'
show_ticket(eac3-ed70/exemplary-hexahedral-needlefish) compiled JSON has no rebar-version key among its fields
src/rebar/_signing_manifest.py:106 REBAR_VERSION_PREFIX = 'rebar-version:' — a SIGNED MANIFEST step (gate-code version), per docs/adr/0064; not a ticket field
'.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/00-bug.yml:19' captures `rebar --version` for GitHub issues, not for rebar tracker tickets
findings.finding: Approach action (b) asserts a reported-against version can be read from 'the tracker ticket's rebar-version field', but rebar tracker tickets carry no rebar-version field; the only 'rebar-version:' in the repo is the gate-code version stamp inside a signed attestation manifest, and the 'rebar --version' capture lives in the GitHub issue template, not on a rebar ticket.
scenarios: An agent following Step 0 looks for a rebar-version field on a claimed ticket and finds none, leaving the reported-against SHA undetermined and the git-log diff-range step (b) unrunnable
findings.suggested_fix: Reword (b) to source the reported-against version only from the report body's `rebar --version`/commit SHA (as the GitHub bug template captures), and define a fallback (e.g. the ticket's CREATE-commit SHA) rather than a nonexistent ticket field.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct mechanism (b)'s version source: rebar tickets have no `rebar-version` field — point to the `rebar --version`/commit-sha in the report's environment section (per .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/00-bug.yml) and to the ticket description text, not a nonexistent ticket field.

findings.finding: Mechanism (b) instructs the agent to read the reported-against version from 'the tracker ticket's rebar-version field', but rebar tickets expose no such field. `rebar-version` is a signing/attestation-manifest stamp (src/rebar/_signing_manifest.py:106, rebar.llm.plan_review.manifest), not a bug-report field; show_ticket output for a real bug ticket contains no rebar-version. The genuine source is the bug issue template's free-text environment field capturing `rebar --version` (.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/00-bug.yml:19,27,29).

findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'the tracker ticket's `rebar-version` field' with 'the `rebar --version` / commit sha recorded in the report's environment section (per the bug issue template), falling back to the sha in the ticket description'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Scope mechanism (a)'s claim to the duplicate class it actually addresses (tickets already present when the debug agent starts) and explicitly defer burst/concurrent same-title duplicates to exemplary-hexahedral-needlefish, per its measured 171s-window finding.
evidence: exemplary-hexahedral-needlefish Phase-1 comment: 'Every same-title true duplicate was created within 171 seconds of its twin... At the instant agent A ran its pre-create search, ticket B did not yet exist... could not have applied.'
Plan: '25 of 221 ... were duplicates or were refuted ... because the agent diagnosed against a stale local tree or a ticket that already existed'
Plan mechanism (a): 'rebar search ...; an existing ticket is linked or resumed instead of filed'
findings.finding: Mechanism (a)'s tracker search targets the 'duplicate/refuted' portion of the named problem, but the complementary task's own measured Phase-1 finding shows the same-title duplicate class was created in concurrent bursts (all 7 within 171s) where a pre-existing search 'could not have applied'. A debug-time Step 0 search catches tickets that ALREADY exist when the agent starts (a real subset), but the plan should not claim it addresses the burst-duplicate cases that motivate the sibling task.
scenarios: Reviewers/operators expect Step 0 to cut the 11% duplicate/refutation rate, but the burst-created same-title duplicates (the class the sibling task measured) are structurally unreachable by a debug-time search
